Ringmer Primary and Nursery School
Welcome!
On behalf of the learners, staff, and governors, I am delighted to welcome you to our website. It is a genuine privilege to lead such a committed and talented team and to work alongside our enthusiastic, motivated learners every day.
Ringmer Primary and Nursery School sits at the heart of a thriving village community. We welcome children from ages 2 to 11 and are proud to have around 350 learners on roll. In recent years, the school has undergone a significant transformation, with rebuilding and refurbishment resulting in a modern, well-equipped environment that supports outstanding learning experiences.
At the centre of everything we do is one clear and unwavering focus: the children.
We believe that children thrive when they are happy, safe, and celebrated for their achievements. Our school values—Respect, Responsibility, Courage, and Compassion—are more than words; they guide our behaviour, shape our learning culture, and help prepare our pupils for life beyond the classroom.
We are deeply committed to inclusion and to helping every child reach their full potential. While we place strong emphasis on high standards in English and Maths, we also offer a rich, engaging, and creative curriculum that inspires curiosity and a love of learning. We want every child to go home buzzing with stories of the exciting learning they’ve experienced.
We believe that education is most successful when it’s a partnership between school and home. Parents and carers are an essential part of each child’s journey, and we are proud of the strong relationships we build with our families. Our open-door policy means we are always here to talk, support, and celebrate progress together.
Above all, our priority is that every child feels valued, supported, and empowered to succeed. When children feel safe and inspired, they become lifelong learners.
I hope you enjoy exploring our website and find the information you need. If you have any questions, please don’t hesitate to contact our school office. And if you see me at the school gate, do come and say hello—I’d be delighted to share more about our wonderful school with you in person.
We currently have limited places available in our Nursery. If you’d like to see what makes Ringmer Primary and Nursery School so special, please contact us to arrange a visit—I’d love to show you around.

Education for a Connected World
The Education for a Connected World framework describes the Digital knowledge and skills that children and young people should have the opportunity to develop at different ages and stages of their lives. It highlights what a child should know in terms of current online technology, its influence on behaviour and development, and what skills they need to be able to navigate it.
The document supports one of the key aims of the government’s Internet Safety Strategy of supporting children to stay safe and make a positive contribution online, as well enabling teachers to develop effective strategies for understanding and handling online risks.

Requests to Withdraw a pupil from RE lessons
Parents have the statutory right under Section 71 of the School Standards and Framework Act 1998 to request their child/ren are wholly or partly excused from:
RE lessons in accordance with the schools’ basic curriculum
Acts of Collective Worship in schools
As parents, you do not have to provide a reason for requesting the withdrawal. However before exercising any right of withdrawal we would recommend you discuss your concerns with the Headteacher.
Important - limitations to withdraw
If pupils are withdrawn from RE, schools have a duty to supervise them, though not to provide additional teaching. A pupil may be required to work in another area of the school, such as the library/shared area.
Whilst parents or carers have a right to withdraw children from RE, they should note that child/ren may also encounter religions and beliefs and wider aspects of faith in other areas of the National Curriculum from which there is no right of withdrawal.
On occasion, spontaneous questions about religious matters are raised by pupils or issues related to religion arise in other curriculum subjects such as history or PSHE. For example, schools promote community cohesion and help pupils to understand ideas about identity and diversity, feelings and emotions within both religious and non-religious contexts.
Managing the Right of Withdrawal
All requests for withdrawals should be made in writing, addressed to the headteacher.
If pupils are withdrawn from RE, schools have a duty to supervise them, though not to provide additional teaching or to incur extra cost. Pupils will usually remain on school premises where it is feasible and appropriate.
Where a request for withdrawal is made, the school must comply and excuse the pupil until the request is rescinded. Though not legally required, it is good practice for a headteacher to invite parents to discuss their written request.
(Section 71(3), School Standards and Framework Act 1998).

Parent Helpers and Volunteers
Join Our Volunteer Family!
Our school thrives on the energy of our parents and local community. At Ringmer, we’re incredibly lucky to have volunteers who share their time and talents to help our learners grow. Whether you’re interested in listening to readers, sharing your math expertise, or assisting in the library, your support has a great impact.
Another way to get involved is to be a helper on a school trip or support extracurricular projects, such as the Year 6 PATINA workshops and hands-on DT activities like sewing or baking
To ensure our school remains a safe environment, all volunteers complete a quick onboarding process (DBS check, references, and safeguarding forms) before starting.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ringmer Primary & Nursery School - Core Principles
pageCache.text:
Core Principles
Curriculum Core Principles
At the heart of our school are our learning principles—the values that drive everything we do.
Each principle is chosen to help our students grow, both academically and personally. Throughout the year, we spotlight different 'drivers' to help children connect their learning to the world around them.
These principles also inspire our teachers to look beyond the classroom, creating vibrant, real-world experiences that make learning unforgettable.
Learning Journeys
Our core principles provide the foundation for everything we teach. To bring our curriculum to life, we use Key Inquiry Questions to drive each topic. Because these questions are explored by everyone from EYFS to Year 6, they act as a golden thread that ties our learning together. This shared focus creates a wonderful opportunity for family conversation; no matter the age of your children, you can explore the same big ideas together at home. While every year group has its own specific curriculum, these questions ensure we are all moving forward as one learning community.
To bring our curriculum to life, we frame every topic with a 'Stunning Start' and a 'Fabulous Finish.' These memorable milestones bookend the learning journey, sparking immediate curiosity and celebrating hard work. To tie it all together, we hold Learning Journey Assemblies at the end of each topic. This is a special time where students from every year group share how they answered the 'Key Question.' We love welcoming parents into school for these celebrations to see first-hand the incredible knowledge our children have discovered.

School Subscriptions
Nessy is an online program designed to support students with their reading, writing and spelling and is particularly good for students with dyslexia or who struggle with literacy.
Over the past two academic years, some of our learners have had access to the following programmes: Nessy Reading and Spelling and Nessy Fingers.
At the end of the last academic year, we made the decision to upgrade our Nessy subscription, which means we now have 300 licences as well as having access to four of their programmes:
